name: Trade war & tariffs
value: Mexico doubling threat 12 Nov; not in force
summary: Trump's 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexico over migrant caravans has not been enacted; Mexico rejected it
state: On 12 Nov President Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods with immediate effect unless Mexico stops migrant caravans; President Sheinbaum rejected the threat, saying no caravan has reached the US border since January 2025 (AP via Spectrum News; Bloomberg). Searches to 23 Nov found no doubled tariff in force and no Mexican retaliation, so Watch holds on the threat.
for_you: Businesses trading with Mexico face uncertainty over possible higher US duties; prices of some imported goods can rise if tariffs change. No action is required of households.
rubric_hit: Watch: new major tariffs threatened between large economies (US threat to double tariffs on Mexico, 12 Nov)

sources.title: Spectrum News (AP) — Sheinbaum rebuffs Trump tariff threat, says no caravans reached U.S. border
Bloomberg — Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexican goods over migrants

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
